questions.question: At what age are university faculty members required to retire compared to staff in central government ministries?
questions.expected_answer: 62 years for university faculty (teachers), compared to 60 years for central government employees
questions.actual_answer: The fifth central pay commission has fixed 60 years for the retirement of central government employees and 62 years for university teachers [1].

questions.question: Can an employee who served for seven years qualify for a central government retirement pension?
questions.expected_answer: No, a minimum of ten years of qualifying service is required to receive a government pension.
questions.actual_answer: No, pension under government is payable to those who have rendered a minimum of ten years qualifying service [1].

questions.question: What is the statutory ceiling on gratuity payments under the 1972 Gratuity Act?
questions.expected_answer: Rs two lakh (calculated at fifteen days' wages per completed year of service)
questions.actual_answer: The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 provides for payment of gratuity subject to a maximum of rupees two lakh [2].

questions.actual_answer: For pensioners not covered by the Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS), the Fifth Pay Commission suggested a medical allowance of Rs. 100 per month [1].

questions.question: Did the Supreme Court characterize pensions as a discretionary bounty or employer grace in the Nakara ruling?
questions.expected_answer: No, the Court held that pension is neither a bounty nor a matter of grace or ex-gratia payment, but a payment for past services rendered.
questions.actual_answer: No, the Supreme Court held in the Nakara ruling that pension is neither a bounty nor a matter of grace depending upon the sweet will of the employer [1], [2].
